ledger.note: 1530: Matamba first appears in the record. 'The first documentary mention of the Kingdom of Matamba is a reference to it giving tribute' to the King of Kongo in 1530; the lead dates the state 'pre-1550-1744'. The page adds 'it does not seem likely that Kongo had any more than a light and symbolic presence in Matamba'. 1530 is a documentary date, not a founding (confidence 1); the page (re-read in the fix pass) gives nothing earlier. [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: region redrawn without the Lukala side.]

region.text: the upper Kwango band of the Baixa de Cassange where Kasanje's Imbangala band settled

ledger.note: 1620: Kasanje takes ground that Matamba claims. The page has Kasanje's Imbangala band, which 'deserted the Portuguese', attack Matamba in the late 1610s-1620 (the Kasanje page dates the state's formation to 1620); Njinga made 'several wars against Kasanje especially in 1634-5', Francisco was 'involved in a war with neighboring Kasanje' in 1681, and the treaty of 7 September 1683 made Matamba 'acknowledge the independence of Kasanje'. The page records no fighting for the other years, so the span is the unresolved claim (confidence on the span 1). [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: replaces the old 1634-1635 contest pair; the mirror contest events are missing from kingdom-of-kasanje, which is outside this repair pass.]

1631: Nzinga conquers Matamba and joins it to Ndongo. 'Between 1631 and 1635, Nzinga invaded the neighboring Kingdom of Matamba', deposing Queen Mwongo Matamba in 1631; the Matamba page: 'Joined to the Kingdom of Ndongo by Queen Nzinga in 1631' and 'From at least 1631 onward, Njinga made Matamba her capital'. The state and its colour continue under a new dynasty.

The treaty was 'signed 7 September 1683'; Verónica 'accepted nominal vassalage' and the treaty 'agreed to acknowledge the independence of Kasanje' after a war with Kasanje in 1681. 1836: Portugal conquers Matamba. 'The Portuguese defeated Matamba in 1836, and advanced to Kasanje by the middle of the century' (Ambundu page). The Matamba page says only that Matamba 'was integrated into Portuguese Angola in the late nineteenth century' (no year) and a king was crowned around 1810, so 1836 is a floor and a bridging year (confidence 1). notes: Cliopatria has no Matamba. The page gives the lead dates 'pre-1550-1744' and a first mention in 1530; it then narrates events to c. 1810 and a late-19th-century integration without a year, so a gap-filler should date the end of the vassal kingdom and the 'Kasanje independence' of 1683 (what Kasanje had been subject to is not stated). Location: the Baixa de Cassange region of Malanje Province; Malanje Province is the proxy, and the capital coordinates are the gazetteer's Malanje (approximate). The Matamba/Ndongo union is two dossiers here: Ndongo for the Portuguese-client kingdom, Matamba for Nzinga's realm. The vassal tint from 1683 is recorded in the portuguese-angola dossier (vassal_start 1683). Page budget (2-5): two pages. (2) Matamba's capital moves off the gazetteer's Malanje (shared with Kasanje) to a different stand-in point inside the shape. (3) The 1683 vassal_start is added (mirror of portuguese-angola's). (4) The 1744 dissolve is removed: the Matamba, Ana II and Katole pages show a sovereign kingdom after 1744. The end moves to 1836 on the Ambundu page's 'The Portuguese defeated Matamba in 1836', at confidence 1; it disagrees with the Matamba page ('integrated into Portuguese Angola in the late nineteenth century', no year) and with the lead (1744). History of Angola and Britannica give no year. A gap-filler should date the integration; portuguese-angola carries the mirror vassal_end and gain of 1836. (5) Thin item (founding): no page opened gives anything earlier than the 1530 tribute record.]
